thread:
Jordan K: Quick sanity check — I’m trying to switch the inference-gateway svc from NodePort -> ClusterIP and let ALB target the pod IPs (targetType: ip). I hit a flurry of failed healthchecks. Anyone seen this mismatch with our readiness probe port mapping?
Alex P: Are you using externalTrafficPolicy: Local anywhere? ALB healthcheck -> ip targets usually require pod IPs to be directly addressable.
Jordan K: No, it's ClusterIP. The ALB target group is set to ip and health checks hit the pod IP:8080/health. But the k8s Service has port: 443 targetPort: 8443. Probe is on 8080 in the container.
Megan L: ahhh, that explains fails. ALB healthchecks to ip:port go to the node ENI -> routes to pod IP. If Service port != probe targetPort, the kube-proxy forwarding can mess with things. For ip target type ALB will call the pod IP directly, bypassing Service port translation. So healthcheck port must match container's host port (i.e., pod containerPort) not the Service port.
Priya S: Also check whether your pods are behind a sidecar (istio/envoy). The ALB healthcheck needs to hit the sidecar or have the sidecar respond.
Jordan K: We're not on Istio. Here's the Service manifest and TF change I'm trying:
```yaml
# k8s svc snippet
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway
  namespace: inference
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: alb
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: ip
spec:
  type: ClusterIP
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8443
  selector:
    app: inference-gateway
```
And Terraform I changed the aws_lb_target_group to port = 8080 for the healthcheck.
Alex P: If target_type = ip and your container listens on 8080 for health, either change the K8s Service targetPort to 8080 or have a readiness probe on 8443 that proxies to 8080. Simpler: set targetPort: 8080.
Megan L: Another nuance: if you're using NodeLocal DNS or hostNetwork the pod IP reachability differs. Confirm the pod IPs are in the target group and healthy in console -> target failed reason (connection refused vs timeout).
Jordan K: Console shows \"health check failed: connection timed out\" for target 10.0.5.12:8080. cURL from node to podIP:8080 times out too. From node to podIP:8443 works. So container isn't binding 8080 — I thought the health endpoint was on 8080.
Priya S: Could be that the container runs ingress TLS termination on 8443 and the app health on /health over that port. If so, you can't point the ALB healthcheck to 8080.
Jordan K: Ok, quick plan: revert TF change (tg port 8080) -> set TG to 8443 and make health check path /ready (HTTPS). Or change Service targetPort to 8443 and keep ALB TG port as 8443. Thoughts?
Alex P: That sounds sane. If you use HTTPS health checks, make sure the TG has a proper ssl policy and healthcheck protocol = HTTPS. ALB needs certs unless you set healthcheck to HTTP on port 80 (not applicable).
Megan L: Also double-check security groups: ALB SG must allow to nodes/pod IPs on that port. We had a case where SG allowed 8443 from ALB, but nodes had host firewall blocking.
Jordan K: Good call. I'll run these steps: 1) roll back TG port->8080; 2) ensure TG protocol=HTTPS and health path=/ready; 3) set service targetPort=8443 if not already; 4) verify SGs and node reachability.
deploy-bot: deployment inference-gateway/ canary -> promoted to stable (image: inference-gw:v2.7.1)
Priya S: If you want to avoid downtime, consider creating a second TG target group pointing at ip:8443 and testing there before switching listeners.
Jordan K: Doing that now. Will post results. Thanks all :thumbsup:
Alex P: If it still fails, paste output of `kubectl get endpoints -n inference inference-gateway -o yaml` and `kubectl describe pod` so we can see ports and readiness.
Jordan K: Will do — update in ~15m.
Megan L: small add — if you later want TLS passthrough (ALB does TLS termination usually), note ALB doesn't support passthrough to pod; you'd need NLB with targetType ip + tls passthrough or use TCP listener and certs on backend. Keep that in mind for cert rotation plan.
Jordan K: Noted. Thanks everyone.
Jordan K: update: test TG with 8443 + HTTPS + /ready -> targets now healthy. Changing TF to point listener -> new TG in a canary listener rule. All good.
